purpose: Manual black-box process-tree-kill interruption of install.ps1 against the exact candidate archive, on native Windows 11, targeting an isolated install root outside any repository or real Latchkit installation.

attempts.target: latchkit sync (7 skills, 2 providers, ~22 files) against an isolated project
attempts.method: Start-Process the launcher, wait 1-15ms, taskkill /T /F the launched process
attempts.outcome: The sync (private Node startup plus file writes) completed before the kill reached the process; no interruption was captured at this operation size. latchkit recover --dry-run / latchkit recover ran cleanly afterward (state: none) both times.
attempts.conclusion: inconclusive for this specific operation; too fast to interrupt externally on this host

attempts.target: install.ps1 fresh install (full bundle stage: private Node runtime, compiled app, node_modules, docs) into a new isolated root
attempts.method: Start-Process install.ps1, wait 1500ms of an observed ~4.8s full run, taskkill /T /F the process tree (confirmed 3 processes terminated)
attempts.outcome: The target root was left with no 'current' activation pointer, an empty versions/ list, and only an abandoned dot-prefixed '*.staging' directory alongside it. self inspect --install-root reported active: null, versions: [], matching a clean, non-broken pre-installation state -- not a partially activated one.
attempts.conclusion: captured; confirmed atomic stage-then-activate behavior under a genuine external kill

recovery.action: re-ran install.ps1 with the same arguments against the same interrupted root
recovery.result: completed normally: active became 1.0.0-win32-x64, launcher reported version 1.0.0

limitations: Only the installation-manager's staging path was exercised for a genuine mid-operation kill; project-level sync/remove interruption was attempted but completed too quickly on this host to catch externally.

Deterministic (non-timing-based) interruption/recovery fault-injection for project mutations, task-state persistence, and worktree cancellation is covered by the source regression suite (node --test), which passed in full during this qualification's npm test run -- see 'atomic termination recovery keeps the last checkpoint...', 'interrupted persistence never partially commits a record...', and 'cancellation records a recovery location and preserves staged, untracked, and ignored task work' in that run's output.
